sources.locator: Theorem2.4.2, printed pp.50–51; §§2.6–2.7, printed pp.59–67, especially Proposition2.7.6, printed pp.66–67. Adjacent visible results and extra §5.1 locator-check material are separately dispositioned below.

contents.name: Smooth Jordan-disk extension with prescribed boundary collars and positive interior germ (local synthesis)
contents.locator: Wall Theorem2.4.2, printed pp.50–51 (PDF58–59), and Proposition2.7.6, printed pp.66–67 (PDF74–75); exact new claim and proof in helper Statement and steps1.1–6.1.
contents.reason: One new draft helper assembles the already-proved local disk-attachment and compact-source extension interfaces with independently written finite planar, collar, angular, and germ arguments. Wall does not state this complete helper; no source theorem is used in place of its local proof.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Theorem2.4.2: Diffeotopy Extension Theorem
contents.reason: The needed compact-source, boundaryless-target, support-controlled interface is already proved locally by lem-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-source-with-boundary. The helper invokes that exact supplier as F5 for a compact annulus and compact disks. No stronger arbitrary-support or target-boundary version is imported.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected
current_helper_uses: step6.1: interior disk translations and germ correction

contents.name: Lemma2.4.1: diffeotopy is an equivalence relation; normalized concatenation
contents.reason: The helper explicitly makes time parameters constant near endpoints/joins before finite concatenation. This elementary normalization is supplied in steps5.1 and6.1; a separate equivalence-relation item is unnecessary for the approved reconstruction scope.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Corollaries2.4.3–2.4.4: compact submanifold isotopy extension, including ambient boundary avoidance
contents.reason: The helper uses only the compact full-dimensional source in an open plane neighborhood, covered by its published F5 supplier. These corollaries confirm that interface; they do not add an independent prerequisite or new result to the page.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.4.5: extension of an isotopy of the entire ambient boundary
contents.reason: The proof works in an ambient boundaryless plane and fixes the middle boundary circle pointwise through F5. It does not require an arbitrary moving ambient-boundary diffeotopy theorem.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Theorem2.4.6: extension for compactly supported isotopies in manifolds with boundary
contents.reason: All actual F5 applications have boundaryless target neighborhoods. General target-boundary extension is broader than the required claim and is not silently assumed.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.4.7: enlargement of a compact submanifold with boundary
contents.reason: Collar maps are extended across their middle circle using the local smooth-extension convention and finite chart cutoffs in step5.1; this separate general submanifold-enlargement result is unnecessary.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Theorem2.3.8: tubular neighborhoods for submanifolds in a manifold with boundary
contents.reason: This adjacent result was visible and read, but step1.1 constructs the needed two-sided normal annulus directly by Euclidean IFT and compactness. The general boundary-adapted tubular-neighborhood theorem is not used.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.5.10: compatible partial tubular neighborhoods of nested submanifolds
contents.reason: No nested arbitrary-codimension tubular-neighborhood extension is required. Finite disk-band charts and the normal-circle collar are explicitly constructed locally.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Lemma2.5.11: oriented local disk-pair embeddings and their isotopy
contents.reason: The general embedding-uniqueness assertion is not used as a shortcut to rotation-system smooth uniqueness. The main proof builds crossing/edge charts, and the helper constructs the actual disk/annulus isotopies it extends.
contents.inspection_scope: Complete brief statement inspected; no proof is supplied on this page.

contents.name: Lemma2.6.1: bicollar of a two-sided corner, unique up to diffeotopy
contents.reason: Only finite planar vertex/edge corner models are needed in step3.1. Compatible strip collars and rounded vertex disks are chosen explicitly there; no global arbitrary-manifold bicollar uniqueness theorem is imported.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.6.2: straightening a two-sided corner, unique up to diffeomorphism
contents.reason: The helper gives the required two-dimensional rounding/displacement and disk-attachment models in steps2.1 and3.1. General corner straightening remains context for the published F4 supplier, not a new prerequisite with an omitted proof.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Lemma2.6.3: introducing a corner and reversing the straightening
contents.reason: The relevant local introduce/glue/round operation is explicitly implemented before F4 is applied in step3.1; the broad ambient-manifold version is not added as a separate item.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.6.4: transverse rounding in a semicollar; explicit smoothing of absolute value
contents.reason: The local graph convolution/cutoff in step2.1 and retained-strip rounding in step3.1 are the special planar operations needed. They are actually written locally and do not rely on an arbitrary topological curve being smoothly approximable.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Corollary2.6.5: a rounded product of disks is a disk
contents.reason: The helper instead verifies its convex rounded triangle is a standard disk by an explicit radial map in step3.1. No general product-of-disks theorem is needed.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Lemma2.7.1: the gluing manifold is independent of chosen collars
contents.reason: The exact collar-identification correction required here is proved by interpolation and published isotopy extension in helper step5.1. Main step2.2 glues maps that agree on actual collars, so it does not assume the general gluing-independence theorem without proof.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Lemma2.7.2: attaching an entire boundary product collar preserves diffeomorphism type
contents.reason: This is part of Wall’s proof context for the disk-unit Proposition2.7.6. The actual library interface consumed is the already-published disk-attachment supplier F4; the helper does not separately import the entire-boundary collar theorem.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.7.3: cutting and gluing recover the original smooth manifold
contents.reason: The finite planar attachment models in helper step3.1 and agreement on genuine collars in main step2.2 provide the needed instances. No new general cutting/gluing theorem is claimed.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Theorem2.7.4: connected sum is determined up to diffeomorphism, with orientation alternatives
contents.reason: Interior connected sums and their classification are not involved in the planar disk/collar reconstruction proof.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.7.5: boundary sum is determined by its summands and orientation data
contents.reason: Only attachment of a disk as the boundary-sum unit is used, via the exact local F4 supplier. Classification of arbitrary summands is unnecessary.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Proposition2.7.6, disk boundary-sum unit: M + D^m is diffeomorphic to M
contents.locator: §2.7, printed pp.66–67 (PDF74–75), including the complete proof using a product disk and collar absorption.
contents.reason: This exact disk-unit operation is already supplied by lem-boundary-connected-sum-with-a-disk-does-not-change-the-diffeomorphism-type. F4 applies it to every rounded triangular cap and tree leaf disk-and-band attachment; the helper retains AC_omega through that published supplier.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: Other assertions of Proposition2.7.6: commutativity, associativity, interior sphere unit, boundary connected-sum formula
contents.reason: These parts of the same inspected proposition are not used in the source repair. Their exclusion is separate from inclusion of the disk boundary-sum unit; no scope or theorem coverage is inferred for them.
contents.inspection_scope: complete relevant statement and proof inspected

contents.name: §2.8 source-history and compact-support caveat
contents.locator: §2.8, printed p.67 (PDF75), beginning of Notes on Chapter2.
contents.reason: The source explicitly warns that compact-support restrictions on diffeotopy extension matter. The helper checks compact annulus/disk source and track support before invoking F5. The global plane rescaling path in main step4.1 is explicitly constructed and does not invoke a compact-support extension theorem.
contents.inspection_scope: Relevant source-history and compact-support caution paragraphs inspected; this is editorial context, not an additional proved result.
